lesson.subtitle: Lesson 28 -- Presentations II: Data and Closing (So, As a Result, However, Although)
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rafael Gasparelli Lima | Lesson 28 -- The Data and the Close
lesson.grammar_point: linking words for result and contrast: so, as a result, however, although

listenings.text: When you show a graph, please don't read every number. Your audience can see the numbers. Your job is to tell the story. First, say what the graph shows. For example: this graph shows our sales from January to June. Then talk about the trend. Is the line going up, going down, or is it steady? After that, point to the important moments, like a peak or a sharp drop, and explain why. Was it because of the weather, or because of a new client? Finally, close your presentation well. Give one key takeaway, say thank you, and invite questions. And please, don't finish with: that's it. Finish with your main message.

Now, let's look at this graph. It shows our fruit imports from Brazil in 2026. From January to March, the line is steady: about two hundred containers a month. However, in April there is a sharp increase, because of the mango season. Imports reach a peak in May, with three hundred and fifty containers. After that, there is a slight drop in June and July. As a result, we have some free space in our warehouses this summer. So, to sum up, the trend is positive, and we want more fruit from Brazil next year. Thank you for your attention. Are there any questions?

extra_audio.text: First, say what the graph shows. Then, describe the general trend. Next, point to the peak and to any sharp drop. After that, explain why, with because of or as a result. Finally, give one key takeaway and invite questions.
